content:
If you are a heavy user of Apple Watch apps, you may have noticed during this summer's beta testing that some existing apps cannot launch on watchOS 27. Apple has identified the issue and is automatically updating apps on behalf of developers to ensure compatibility.

These updates will be pushed through the App Store, with the release notes reading: "This app has been updated by Apple to prepare for compatibility with watchOS 27. No new features added."

Apple notified developers this week that the process will be completed by August 31.

watchOS 27 (along with iOS 27 and all other new operating systems) is expected to be released to the public around mid-September, so the necessary updates are being pushed out in time.

Apple said that due to issues with the arm64 portion of some watchOS apps, this handling is required. It sounds like they are automatically reprocessing and repackaging the apps to fix binary compatibility issues, allowing existing apps to continue functioning normally without developers having to take any action.
